mortgage.title: 30 years, 10% down and manual PMI
mortgage.inputs: Home price $375,000; 10% down; 6% interest over thirty years; annual property tax $4,800, homeowners insurance $1,800 and HOA $1,200; manually entered PMI $1,500 annually for eleven years. No extra principal or cost growth.
steps: Down payment is $37,500, leaving $337,500 of principal.
Apply the monthly fixed-payment formula, then add tax, homeowners insurance, HOA and entered PMI divided by twelve.
Compare both monthly obligations and the cash down payment against the 20%-down scenario. PMI is a manual hypothetical input.

mortgage.title: 30 years, tax and insurance rise 3%
mortgage.inputs: Home price $375,000; 20% down; 6% fixed interest over thirty years. Initial annual tax $4,800 and homeowners insurance $1,800 each rise 3% after each twelve payments; HOA remains $1,200 annually. No PMI or extra principal.
steps: Keep scheduled principal and interest unchanged.
At month thirteen, multiply the first-year property tax and insurance amounts by 1.03 and add unchanged HOA.
Read the month-thirteen schedule total separately from the initial monthly result. Loan-year cost growth is not an escrow prediction.

401k.title: 50% of first 3%
401k.inputs: Age 35; annual salary $80,000; employer matches 50% of the first 3% of employee pay contributed. No second match tier; use the fixed 2026 limits and equal-payroll assumptions.
steps: Employee contribution needed for the full stated match is $80,000 × 3% = $2,400.
The employer match is 1.5% of pay. Credited matching does not establish vested ownership or a tax result.

balance-transfer.title: 12-month promotion, financed fee
balance-transfer.inputs: Transfer $6,000. Use a $350 fixed monthly payment, financed 3% transfer fee, 0% APR for twelve months and 24% thereafter; compare with keeping the original balance at 24% APR.
steps: Add each financed fee to its opening balance exactly once.
Charge monthly APR/12 interest at the applicable promotional or later rate, then subtract the capped monthly payment.
Compare interest plus the one-time fee under the same monthly budget; review remaining balances at the end of each promotion.

balance-transfer.title: Two offers: 3% / 18 months vs 5% / 24 months
balance-transfer.inputs: Transfer $6,000. Use $250 monthly for both offers. A charges 3%, with 0% APR for eighteen months; B charges 5%, with 0% for twenty-four months. Both later APRs are 24%, and fees are financed.
steps: Add each financed fee to its opening balance exactly once.
Charge monthly APR/12 interest at the applicable promotional or later rate, then subtract the capped monthly payment.
Compare interest plus the one-time fee under the same monthly budget; review remaining balances at the end of each promotion.
